headline: Land development rule changes on rare species, accessory dwellings, and form-based code advanced; bedrock removal failed 3-2.
summary: Under the rare species rules, land disturbance within 500 feet of mapped rare, threatened, or endangered species or significant natural communities in the Tier 1A area would need review. Lots under half an acre with an existing principal building, and no species confirmed there in 25 years, are exempt. Other changes reconnect form-based code standards to city-wide rules and remove accessory dwelling unit wording that conflicts with the state definition.
decisions: Failed 3-2 to approve LDR 26-01 on bedrock removal and advance it to City Council.
Approved LDR 26-09, as amended tonight, and advanced it to City Council.
Approved LDR 26-11 and advanced it to City Council.
Approved LDR 26-12 and advanced it to City Council.
discussion: Rare species rules: Members asked how the administrative officer would judge whether a project could affect a species, and whether that decision could be appealed. Fish and Wildlife could give a quick yes or no when the officer is unsure, and an officer's decision can be appealed to the DRB.
Bedrock removal rule: The rule was split from the other amendments at a member's request, and the motion to advance it failed 3-2.
October 27 minutes: Members said the October 27 vote already advanced the bedrock removal rule, and it will go to City Council with the other amendments.
